studies.Study: Kurahashi N et al. (2009) [PMID: 19068095] — estimate 1 · Male
studies.Reference: Coffee, green tea, and caffeine consumption and subsequent risk of bladder cancer in relation to smoking status: a prospective study in Japan.
studies.Title: Coffee, green tea, and caffeine consumption and subsequent risk of bladder cancer in relation to smoking status: a prospective study in Japan.
studies.Authors: Kurahashi N, Inoue M, Iwasaki M, Sasazuki S, Tsugane S, Japan Public Health Center (JPHC) Study Group
studies.Population: Japanese men and women aged 40-69 years
studies.comparison_type: Highest versus lowest category of caffeine consumption

sample_size.excerpt: We conducted a population-based prospective study in a cohort of Japanese, comprising a total of 49 566 men and 54 874 women aged 40–69 years who reported their coffee and green tea consumption at baseline.
sample_size.location: abstract; total_n derived from reported group counts 49566 + 54874 = 104440

cases.excerpt: During follow-up from 1990 through 2005, 164 men and 42 women were newly diagnosed with bladder cancer.
cases.location: abstract; cases derived from reported group counts 164 + 42 = 206

effect_size.excerpt: When stratified by smoking status, coffee and caffeine consumption were associated with an increased risk of bladder cancer in never- or former-smoking men, with hazard ratios (95% confidence interval) in the highest categories of coffee (one or more cups per day) and caffeine consumption compared with the lowest of 2.24 (95% CI = 1.21–4.16) and 2.05 (95% CI = 1.15–3.66), respectively.

confidence_interval.excerpt: When stratified by smoking status, coffee and caffeine consumption were associated with an increased risk of bladder cancer in never- or former-smoking men, with hazard ratios (95% confidence interval) in the highest categories of coffee (one or more cups per day) and caffeine consumption compared with the lowest of 2.24 (95% CI = 1.21–4.16) and 2.05 (95% CI = 1.15–3.66), respectively.

sample_size.excerpt: A total of 826 histologically verified cancer cases were individually matched by age, sex, and area of residence to 792 randomly selected population controls.
